title: Nightshift SRE on-call scratchpad — Miguel
content:
2026-03-13 night shift notes (fragile, quick, actionable)

00:47 UTC — Pager: increased 5xx rate from hosted API region-us-west-2 (alert: api-5xx-rate-high).
- Initial triage: error spikes align with a deploy window (2026-03-13 00:40 UTC) on runtime v2.14.
- Quick checks: infra hosts healthy, GPU ci nodes show normal load, queue depth spiked on the routing layer.
- Mitigation: rolled back routing change in canary (git tag: routing-fallback-2026-03-13), 5xx rate dropped to baseline by 00:54 UTC.
- Follow-ups: CRA-1 (cause analysis) assigned to @Aisha — see INF-4721.

01:10 — Paging notes to add to postmortem:
- Root cause hypothesis: buggy predicate in smart-routing that forwarded short-lived traffic to a model variant that lacked a compatibility shim -> NPE in runtime path.
- Why rollback helped: reverting to previous routing config avoided variant selection path.
- Impact: ~14 minutes of elevated 5xx for 2% of requests in us-west-2; no data exfiltration, no durability loss.

Runbook TODOs (short, actionable) — strike-through when done:
- [ ] Update routing runbook step 2 to include "verify compatibility shim presence" and expected log lines (owner: Miguel).
- [ ] Add explicit canary metric for variant-compatibility failures (owner: Platform Observability).
- [ ] Create a small e2e test that simulates variant mismatch during canary deploys (owner: eng-serving-runtime).
- [ ] Add a quick rollback command alias in the ops-cli (pr candidate: ops/cli#342).

Notes for handoff (to morning shift):
- Created a short incident timeline and pinned to INF-4721 (check comments).
- Aisha is prepping initial RCA draft; she flagged a secondary issue: stale cache TTLs allowed an invalid variant mapping to persist for ~9s.
- Action for SRE morning: validate that cache TTL default config was updated in deploy pipeline (pipeline: infra-cfg).

Monitoring & metrics to watch in next 24h:
- api.5xx.rate (region: us-west-2) — threshold 0.5% over baseline.
- routing.variant-compatibility.errors — new metric to add; currently emits as runtime.error with tag=variant_mismatch.
- p95 latency for short requests (<128 tokens) — spike correlated earlier.

Small troubleshooting snippets I ran:
- curl health endpoints on canary /live -> 200 OK, but logs showed stack traces referencing compatibility.go:line 138.
- kubectl logs routing-canary -n runtime | grep "variant_mismatch" | head -n 10 -> saw 16 occurrences.

Unresolved questions (to capture in RCA):
- Why didn't the compatibility shim get packaged into variant v1.3.2? (buildstep artifact mismatch?)
- Are there CI gates that should have caught the missing binary? (owner: release-engineering)

Quick checklist for sprint tasks (non-blocking for production):
- [ ] Add integration test for variant packaging (low priority, Sprint 22).
- [ ] Investigate whether the model catalog UI can display "compatibility status" flag for each variant.
- [ ] Short writeup for product explaining the incident in plain terms (no internal stack traces).

Personal notes / reminders to self:
- Keep incident timeline terse; include symptom -> mitigation -> RCA plan.
- Be explicit about what changed in routing config and what the safe rollback is.
- Follow up with Release Eng tomorrow about artifact signing (possible culprit).

Misc quick references (commands I used):
- ops-cli rollback routing canary --env=us-west-2 --reason="variant mismatch"
- kubectl -n runtime logs deploy/routing-canary --since=15m | grep variant_mismatch
- prometheus query: increase(rate(api_5xx_total[1m])) by (region)

End-of-shift status:
- Incident mitigated and stable.
- Postmortem ticket created (INF-4721).
- Runbook updates scheduled and assigned.

If morning team needs anything urgent: ping me directly in slack @miguel (I check morning channel at 08:30 local).

---

Random scratch ideas (for later):
- Add a pre-deploy compatibility smoke test that runs a tiny request through the full routing selection stack (cheap, <100ms).
- Consider a metric that counts "deploys with compatibility warnings" and surfaces in Console rollout page.

End of notes.
